title: Adaptive burst absorber and hint-driven kernel allocator
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement an adaptive "burst absorber" admission layer combined with a hint-driven kernel allocator to reduce tail latency during short request spikes and improve overall token throughput. This ticket focuses on coordinating prefill/admission decisions with kernel selection signals (attention profile and sequence length histogram) to avoid pathological kernel switches mid-decode and to smooth microburst-induced latency spikes.

Background: We observe 95th/99th percentile latency regressions during ad-hoc microbursts where many short-prefill requests arrive together. Current admission uses a size-first heuristic which can trigger kernel reconfiguration for nearby batches, causing decoding stalls. Separately, attention-heavy prompts occasionally push the runtime into a slower kernel path for subsequent decodes. The burst absorber will accept short-lived over-capacity by absorbing and reshaping admission windows, while hint-driven kernel allocation aims to steer batches to compatible kernels ahead of decode to avoid mid-decode handoffs.

Goals:
- Reduce 99th percentile end-to-end latency for mixed short/long workloads by 20% under bursty arrival patterns.
- Reduce number of kernel-switch events during ongoing decodes by 80% in the experiment workload.
- Keep median latency and token throughput within 5% of baseline for steady-state traffic.

Non-Goals:
- This ticket does not implement new quantization paths or new kernel implementations; it only coordinates selection and admission.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile latency improves >= 20% on the mixed-bursty benchmark (internal benchmark 'burst-mix-v2') compared to baseline
Kernel-switch events per 10k decodes drops >= 80% in the same benchmark
No more than 5% regression in median latency or overall token throughput under steady traffic
Unit and integration tests covering admission logic, hint propagation, and kernel selection simulation are present
Tooling: dashboard graphs for admission queue depth, absorbed-burst count, and kernel-switch rate added to runtime-1.21 dashboard
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight 'burst absorber' layer that maintains a short (50-200ms) elastic window to accept transient spikes by smoothing admission credits rather than immediately spawning extra kernel reconfigurations

Expose a stable 'kernel-hint' metadata field on prefill requests: enum {FAST_SMALL, ATTENTION_HEAVY, LONG_SEQ}. Hints are best-effort and can be derived from token length, prompt markers, or evaluated on edge heuristics

Kernel allocator matches batches using a two-stage comparator: (1) affinity by hint + recent kernel latency profile, (2) capacity fit. Strictly avoid mid-decode kernel switches by reserving decode slots when a kernel change would be required
Admission policy prioritizes tail SLO-bound requests when customer_impact label is high; otherwise it favors small fast-prefill jobs to keep median latency low
Use probabilistic decay for burst absorber credits so sustained load still respects capacity and triggers autoscaling instead of indefinite absorption
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype in simulator (3 days) to validate absorber window sizes and hint matching thresholds
Phase 2: Runtime implementation behind feature flag 'burst_absorb_v1' and 'kernel_hint_routing' (5 days). Minimal perf-critical path changes; admission decision occurs in admission controller thread
Phase 3: Canary rollout to dedicated test cluster + synthetic bursts (2 days). Collect metrics and validate kernel-switch reduction
Phase 4: Gradual rollout to select host pools, monitor dashboards, iterate on thresholds (3-5 days)
Phase 5: Full rollout gated on metrics and postmortem review
experiments: Synthetic workload 'burst-mix-v2': 95% short-prefill (<30 tokens) with 5% long decodes; inject 10k qps microbursts of 500 concurrent short-prefill arrivals to simulate traffic spikes
Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel_switch_count per 10k decodes, absorbed_burst_count, admission_queue_depth, decode_slot_reservations
Baseline: current admission + kernel selection. Variant A: burst_absorber only. Variant B: kernel_hint_routing only. Variant C: both combined (target)
Preliminary simulator runs show Variant C reduces kernel-switch events by ~83% and 99th latency by ~18% (needs runtime validation).
rollout_plan: Enable feature on canary pool (5% traffic) behind feature flag and runtime flag to disable hint routing
Create alert: kernel_switch_rate > baseline * 0.9 or p99 latency > baseline * 1.1 during canary => automatic rollback
If canary passes for 48 hours with metrics green, expand to dedicated pools with gradual increments (25%, 50%, 100%)
Post-rollout: run a 72-hour stability window and capture traces for any kernel-switch anomalies
Ensure runbook updated with steps to disable burst absorber and to force kernel fallback in emergencies
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Burst absorber may mask sustained overload leading to resource exhaustion. Mitigation: probabilistic decay and hard caps that feed into autoscaler signals
Risk: Hints misclassified could route to suboptimal kernels increasing latency. Mitigation: conservative hint derivation with opt-out and quick rollback; monitor hint_error_rate
Risk: Complexity in admission controller could introduce contention. Mitigation: keep decision path lock-free, micro-benchmark the controller, and fail-open to existing admission policy on timeouts
Risk: Unexpected interaction with Dedicated pool isolation. Mitigation: run dedicated-pool-only canary with isolation flags and validate tenant-aware admission behavior
